title: Scientists Find New Giant Stick Insects in Australia
summary:
Stick insects look just like twigs. Some of them even fooled scientists!

A team from the University of Sydney studied big stick insects in a group called Anchiale. Scientists thought there were only two kinds in Australia. The team found there are really five. They found two new species and brought back a third that had been missed for decades.

The team used DNA tests, museum collections, field trips and sightings shared by the public. One well-known stick insect had been given the wrong name for decades. Now it has its own name, Anchiale robusta.

Another new species, Anchiale mabiensis, lives in the endangered Mabi rainforest in Queensland. Its eggs have a special lid. No one had ever seen that in a stick insect before.

"Taxonomy is often a bit like detective work," said Dr. Braxton Jones. Taxonomy is the science of naming living things.
why_it_matters: Even familiar bugs can hold surprises, so scientists keep studying nature to learn what lives around us.
